key_insight: Combining NLP predictions from radiology Findings and Impressions improved brain metastasis detection over either section alone.
clinical_relevance: The pipeline could help cancer registries track brain metastases arising after cancer diagnosis, which current surveillance often misses.
method: Manually labeled brain/head radiology reports from a population-based Alberta cancer cohort.
Trained separate Bio_ClinicalBERT models on Findings and Impressions using 1,879 samples.
Used the higher section-level probability as the report prediction and validated across three Canadian provinces.
evidence_signal: At a 0.4 threshold, internal validation on 1,833 reports from 357 patients yielded 88.8% sensitivity and 49.9% precision; external sensitivity was 91.8% in Ontario and 72.6% in British Columbia.
watch_item: Modest precision and variable external sensitivity warrant local validation and assessment of false-positive review workload before registry implementation.
paper_title: Natural Language Processing Based Solution for Labeling Brain Metastasis Identified in Radiology Reports
